vpc_topology_notes: Initial preference: multi-AZ VPC with two private subnets per AZ, dedicated NAT gateways for outbound egress, separate management/public subnet for control-plane VPN. Prefer provider-managed transit gateway for inter-region stitching. Customer wants explicit CIDR ranges to avoid overlap with existing corporate VPCs.
inbound_outbound_requirements: Inbound: allow TLS-terminated control-plane from static Redwood egress IPs via customer firewall; customer will open port 443 and a pinned VPN tunnel. Outbound: restrict to specific AWS service endpoints and Redwood-managed logging/KMS endpoints; no unrestricted internet egress from inference nodes. Must support forced egress through customer network firewall for DLP inspection.
kms_integration_expectations: Customer requires BYOK with AWS KMS and HSM-backed key material for model artifact encryption at rest. Wants proof of key rotation workflow and access controls (IAM roles + KMS key policies). Audit trail for key usage is mandatory.
audit_logging_and_residency: Audit logs must be forwarded to customer's CloudWatch/Logging S3 bucket with 7-year retention policy. Data residency: model inputs and logs must remain in eu-west-1 for EU-sensitive tenants; for NA tenants use us-east-1. Redwood Private control plane will be placed in customer's VPC to satisfy residency requirements.
